newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus-Bayer sees 1996 operating profit up.
newsitem.headline: Focus-Bayer sees 1996 operating profit up.

text.p: Germany's Bayer AG on Tuesday said acquisitions helped boost its nine month results, leaving the chemicals and drugs group confident of reaching its 1996 sales target of 47 billion marks ($31.06 billion) and posting a 10 percent rise in operating earnings.
Bayer reported a 12 percent rise in nine-month pre-tax profits to 3.7 billion marks while sales rose 7.4 percent to 36.54 billion marks, broadly in line with forecasts.
Third quarter pre-tax profits climbed 8.3 percent to 981 million marks with sales also rising 8.3 percent to 11.747 billion marks.
Bayer said the jump in nine-month sales was largely fuelled by its acquisitions of a printing plate business, the Florasynth fragrance unit, and the ABS plastics unit.
The group also benefited from more favourable exchange rates after the strong mark had largely dented German companies' results last year. Price increases also contributed to the rise in sales.
Bayer said it was confident it could meet its sales target of 47 billion marks in 1996 after achieving sales of 44.58 billion marks in 1995.
But management board chairman Manfred Schneider said in a speech prepared for a news conference that sales developments were mixed with foreign sales accounting for the lion's share of growth.
Foreign sales rose 10.1 percent in the first nine months while domestic sales climbed only 2.7 percent.

While Bayer said it expected to post a 10 percent rise in operating income for the full year, it also said it expected additional charges in the fourth quarter, due to early retirement, restructuring and other items.

Among its product groups, Bayer said the polymers business grew most strongly, posting a 14.4 percent rise in sales to 7.12 billion marks while health care sales climbed 3.7 percent to 8.676 billion marks.
The group's Agfa photo division also posted strong growth with sales climbing 14.2 percent to 5.576 billion marks.
Bayer is the first of Germany's so called chemical giants to report its nine-month numbers this year.
The company's stock was little moved by the news, with the profit growth marginally at the lower end of analysts' expectations, but was stable at 57.15 marks, up 15 pfennigs, in early bourse trade.
